item.title: Aegean Miles+Bonus Cuts Air China Mileage Earning from October 12, Closes Booking Class P Loophole
item.dc:creator: Peer
item.description: Miles+Bonus, the frequent flyer program of Aegean Airlines, has published an updated earning chart for flights operated by Star Alliance partner Air China. The new accrual rates will take effect for travel from October 12, 2026. Most notably, the updated chart patches a long-standing loophole: in recent years, Air China booking class P was mapped […]
item.content:encoded:
Miles+Bonus, the frequent flyer program of Aegean Airlines, has published an updated earning chart for flights operated by Star Alliance partner Air China. The new accrual rates will take effect for travel from October 12, 2026.

Most notably, the updated chart patches a long-standing loophole: in recent years, Air China booking class P was mapped to first class, earning a 200% mileage credit—even though the carrier long ago transitioned P into an inexpensive economy class fare bucket. First discussed on FlyerTalk in January 2024, travelers routinely collected generous mileage credits on deeply discounted economy tickets.

In total, the following earning changes will apply:

• Booking class A: 200% → 150% (first class)
• Booking class R: 125% → 115% (business class)
• Booking class P: 200% → 25% (economy class, previously mapped as first class)

These updates will be incorporated into wheretocredit.com and our own mileage calculator.

item.content:encoded:
American Express is continuing to expand its Centurion Lounge network. As announced this week, a second lounge is set to open at London Heathrow. In addition, two existing lounges in the US will be significantly expanded:

• London Heathrow: A second Centurion Lounge will open in 2028. It will measure more than 800 m² and be located in Terminal 5 (currently there is only one, in Terminal 3).
• Philadelphia: The existing Centurion Lounge will be renovated and expanded from 550 to 1,100 m² (the lounge will be closed from October 2026 until the end of 2027).
• Houston: Expansion from 740 to 2,140 m², adding an à la carte dining area and a second bar.

Also in the pipeline, though previously announced: a Centurion Lounge in Newark (pushed back to 2027 from 2026), a Sidebar by Centurion in Charlotte (2027), and a Centurion Lounge in Boston (2029).

Source: American Express press release

The cruise price includes full board with breakfast, lunch, and dinner (some specialty restaurants are excluded), as well as cold and hot water, coffee, and tea. Furthermore, TUI’s Premium All-Inclusive concept offers soft drinks, beer, sparkling wine, and a selection of wines, cocktails, long drinks, spirits, coffee specialties, and much more included in the cruise fare.

If you are planning to take a cruise this year from the Canary Islands, we have published a comprehensive guide with all the available options and tips for your stops on each of the islands:

Editor’s Note: With its Premium All-Inclusive package, TUI Cruises is a very cost-effective option compared to its competitors, even if you don’t speak German fluently. This sailing also includes an overnight stay in Madeira, so you can rent a car and explore the island from early in the morning.

Route (Sample Departure: December 10, 2026)

Your cruise begins in the port of Las Palmas on Gran Canaria, heading first toward Fuerteventura. From there, the ship sails to Madeira, staying overnight in Funchal. Following a sea day, the ship calls at Santa Cruz de La Palma, followed by a visit to Tenerife before returning to Gran Canaria.

The Ship

TUI Cruises’ Mein Schiff 7 was built at the Meyer Turku shipyard in Finland and entered service in 2024, making it the cruise line’s first newbuild since 2019. The ship is 316 meters long and 36 meters wide, with room for around 2,900 passengers and up to 1,000 crew members.

New on board are interior and oceanview cabins designed specifically for solo travelers. They are meant to cut the surcharge you’d otherwise pay for single occupancy of a double cabin, while still giving you a private space to retreat and relax at any time.

Mein Schiff 7 has 12 restaurants and bistros covering a wide range of cuisines, including a new Asian and sushi restaurant (at an extra charge) and a restaurant for fans of Italian food. The Premium All-Inclusive concept applies throughout, and food is available 24 hours a day. The specialty restaurants in the Große Freiheit area (such as the steakhouse) are excluded and cost extra. More than 100 brand-name drinks and cocktails are included.

Mein Schiff 7 also offers a wide range of entertainment and leisure activities. The familiar 25-meter pool on the outer deck is back, along with an indoor pool and a large sauna area. In the evenings, a changing line-up of shows provides something for every taste, from music and theater to acrobatics and magic.

TUI Cruises’ newest ship also makes an important statement on sustainability. It runs on lower-emission marine diesel, connects to green shore power in port, and is equipped with high-efficiency catalytic converters.

Destination

Information & Tips for Maldives

The Maldives, a tropical island nation in the Indian Ocean, is known for its overwater bungalows, coral reefs, and clear turquoise waters, making it a popular spot for snorkeling, diving, and beach relaxation. The local currency is the Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR), though US dollars are widely accepted in resorts. Prices tend to be high, especially on private islands, with most essentials and activities geared toward luxury tourism. The weather is warm year-round, averaging around 28–31°C, with a dry season from November to April and a wetter monsoon season from May to October.

Transport in the Maldives is limited and varies depending on the island. There are no cities in the conventional sense—Malé, the capital, is the only urban center and is walkable due to its small size. Getting between islands typically requires travel by speedboat, ferry, or seaplane, depending on distance and location. Public ferries are cheaper but slower and less frequent, while private transfers arranged by resorts are faster but expensive. Overall, getting around can be time-consuming and dependent on weather conditions.

item.title: EU Air Passenger Rights Reform: What Changes with the New Regulation in October 2027
item.dc:creator: Peer
item.description: For years, European Union policymakers have debated a comprehensive overhaul of EU air passenger rights (Regulation EC 261/2004), which first took effect in 2005 and has remained virtually unchanged ever since. The reform is now concrete: in June, the key framework was announced, and the final legislative text has now been published, revealing critical details […]
item.content:encoded:
For years, European Union policymakers have debated a comprehensive overhaul of EU air passenger rights (Regulation EC 261/2004), which first took effect in 2005 and has remained virtually unchanged ever since. The reform is now concrete: in June, the key framework was announced, and the final legislative text has now been published, revealing critical details that were previously missing.

The full amending regulation is accessible on EUR-Lex. The new passenger rights regime will take effect on October 23, 2027. As before, it applies to worldwide flights operated by EU-based airlines, as well as all commercial departures from airports within the EU (+ Norway, Switzerland, and Iceland).

Below, we have summarized the most important aspects of the new regulation, focusing specifically on how they differ from the status quo. For travelers, the outcome is a mixed bag: while several loopholes are closed, certain consumer protections have been noticeably weakened.

Info

This article does not constitute legal advice and represents our editorial analysis of the legislative text. If you spot an inaccuracy or have additional insights, please feel free to leave a comment.

Table of Contents

  • Core Compensation Rules Remain in Place
  • Price Transparency: Fares Must Include a Cabin Bag
  • Positive Changes for Passengers
  • Negative Changes for Passengers
  • Additional Legal Clarifications
  • Our Take

Core Compensation Rules Remain in Place

First, the good news: the cornerstone compensation amounts for flight cancellations and delays remain unchanged. Whenever statutory compensation is due, the compensation tiers remain:

  • €250 for flights ≤ 1,500 kilometers
  • €400 for flights between 1,500 and 3,500 kilometers (as well as longer intra-EU flights)
  • €600 for all other long-haul flights (> 3,500 kilometers)

Statutory care obligations—such as complimentary meals and refreshments during long delays and hotel accommodation in the event of overnight disruption—are also largely preserved, though several important details have been amended.

Price Transparency: Fares Must Include a Cabin Bag

Over the past decade, airlines have steadily unbundled their fare structures. Legacy network carriers like Lufthansa, Air France, KLM, and Finnair have followed budget airlines by offering entry-level tickets that include only a small personal item. Bringing a standard overhead carry-on trolley incurs a surcharge (which balloons if paid at the boarding gate).

Contrary to earlier legislative proposals, unbundled hand-luggage-free tickets are not prohibited. However, the EU is mandating strict upfront price transparency: airlines and booking intermediaries will only be permitted to advertise prices that include one standard piece of carry-on baggage (such as a trolley) and one personal item by default. If overhead bins are full, airlines retain the right to gate-check the trolley into the aircraft hold—provided they do so free of charge.

When offering or publishing air fares, the air fares that include a piece of carry-on baggage shall be displayed by default before the start of any booking process to facilitate fare comparisons between airlines.

This paragraph does not prevent air carriers or intermediaries from offering different price options to passengers who voluntarily travel without carry-on baggage.

EU Regulation 2026/2202, Article 11a

Airlines remain free to offer discounted Basic fares without a large cabin bag. However, they will no longer be allowed to use these stripped-down prices in initial search displays or advertising; they can only present them as opt-out discounts later in the booking funnel. This is likely to curtail the utility of such fares, which primarily existed to gain an artificial advantage on flight metasearch engines before tacking on ancillary bag fees.

The regulation does not prescribe exact maximum weight or dimensional limits for the overhead bag. Only the personal item is explicitly defined: 40 x 30 x 15 cm—or anything that fits under the seat in front.

Positive Changes for Passengers

Beyond hand luggage transparency, several passenger-friendly measures have been codified into law:

  • Free Name Corrections: In the event of minor spelling mistakes or legal name changes (such as through marriage), airlines must correct passenger names free of charge. This right explicitly does not allow transferring a ticket to another person (Article 12a).
  • Right to Adjacent Seating: Passengers traveling with young children, pregnant passengers, or passengers with disabilities have a statutory right to complimentary adjacent seat selection. In addition, these travelers (along with those traveling with strollers or certified service animals) must be offered priority boarding (Article 11).
  • Mandatory Disclosure of Delay Reasons: In the event of flight delays or cancellations, airlines must explicitly inform passengers of the exact operational or weather-related reason for the disruption in writing.
  • No App or Account Requirement: Online check-in must be fully functional without forcing passengers to download an app or register for a user profile. Airlines must provide free printed boarding passes at the airport if the traveler completed check-in online (Article 11b).
  • Return Ticket Protection on Outbound No-Shows: If a passenger books a round-trip ticket and misses or skips the outbound flight, the airline cannot cancel the return journey. The passenger must be transported on the return flight at no additional charge (Article 4(5)).
  • Protection of Scheduled Stopovers: If a traveler books an itinerary with an intentional extended layover, they can insist on routing through that specific transit airport during irregular operations. In other words, they are legally entitled to reject alternative re-routings that bypass their chosen layover city (Article 8(4)).
  • Tarmac Delay Contingency Plans: During tarmac delays, airlines must provide complimentary drinking water, adequate cabin ventilation, and allow passengers to deplane after a maximum of 2 hours on the tarmac (Article 6a).

Negative Changes for Passengers

However, the new legislation also weakens passenger protections in several critical areas:

  • Re-routing Reimbursement Capped at 400%: In the event of a cancellation, airlines remain obligated to offer re-routing at the earliest opportunity. If the carrier fails to offer an alternative within 3 hours, the passenger may book their own replacement ticket. However, the airline is only required to reimburse this alternative up to a maximum cap of 400% of the original ticket price. If a last-minute ticket exceeds this ceiling, the consumer must bear the difference out of pocket. It remains unclear how this cap will be applied to award tickets booked with frequent flyer miles.
  • 50% Compensation Reduction Window Broadened: Airlines can currently cut statutory compensation by 50% if an alternative flight arrives within 2 hours (< 1,500 km), 3 hours (< 3,500 km), or 4 hours (> 3,500 km) of the original schedule. Under the new rules, this buffer is raised to 4 hours across all flight distances. Furthermore, this 50% reduction will now also apply to standard delays under 4 hours (Article 7(2)).
  • Claim Deadline Slashed to 9 Months: Compensation claims must be formally submitted within 9 months of the flight date (Article 7(9)). Previously, national statutes of limitations applied (such as 3 years in Germany or up to 6 years in the UK).
  • Hotel Accommodation Capped at 3 Nights: During extraordinary circumstances (such as volcanic ash clouds or major airspace closures), an airline’s duty of care to provide hotel accommodation is capped at a maximum of three nights (Article 9(6)), with exceptions for passengers with reduced mobility.
  • New Definition of Arrival Time: Decades of court rulings established that arrival time was determined by the moment the aircraft doors opened at the gate. The new regulation defines arrival time as “on-block” time—the moment the parking brakes are engaged (Article 1(2)(d)(x)). While this represents a difference of only a few minutes, it could prevent borderline flights from reaching the critical 3-hour compensation threshold.

Additional Legal Clarifications

The new legal framework also codifies several gray areas that previously relied on fragmented court rulings:

  • Codification of European Case Law: The original text of Regulation 261/2004 only explicitly mentioned compensation for cancellations and denied boarding. Decades of European Court of Justice (ECJ) rulings established that delays of 3+ hours qualify for compensation as well. Formally writing this into statute is particularly beneficial for travelers in Switzerland, which applies EU air passenger rules but is not bound by ECJ case law.
  • Clarification on Downgrade Compensation: If a passenger is involuntarily downgraded (e.g. from business class to economy class), airlines must refund up to 75% of the ticket price excluding government taxes. Several airlines previously argued that carrier-imposed surcharges were exempt from this refund. The text clarifies that the base fare includes carrier surcharges, provided those surcharges vary depending on the cabin class booked (Article 10).
  • Strict Definition of Extraordinary Circumstances: Annex 1 establishes a comprehensive list of what constitutes an extraordinary circumstance. Third-party airport ground handler strikes qualify as extraordinary if the airline has no control over the provider. By contrast, internal airline crew strikes remain strictly non-extraordinary.
  • Airport Emergency Plans: Major European airports (handling > 4 million passengers per year) must develop formal contingency plans. When activated during mass disruptions, airlines are granted extended deadlines to process refunds.
  • Earlier Re-routing Permitted: Re-routing on an earlier flight is now formally recognized with passenger consent. In such cases, compensation may be reduced by 25% or 50% (Articles 8 & 7(3)).
  • Mandatory Disclosure of Separate Tickets: Online travel agencies (and carriers) must explicitly warn consumers if an itinerary consists of separate, unprotected tickets (such as “virtual interlining” on Kiwi.com). This curtails recent court rulings that held initial airlines liable for missed onward connections on separate tickets (Article 14(2)–(3)).
  • Regular 5-Year Inflation Reviews: The European Commission will publish a comprehensive review of air passenger rights every five years, assessing whether statutory compensation figures should be adjusted for inflation (Article 17).

Our Take

The revised EU passenger rights regulation represents a pragmatic compromise that largely maintains Europe’s strong consumer protections. The carry-on bag transparency rule is a welcome step forward: it restores meaningful price comparison across metasearch engines without outlawing low-cost business models. It remains to be seen whether ultra-low-cost carriers will attempt to circumvent it through new booking funnel gimmicks.

However, one provision is difficult to defend: capping self-rebooking reimbursement at 400% of the original ticket price. If a consumer books an economy class ticket across Europe for €20 and the flight is cancelled, finding a last-minute same-day alternative easily costs €300 to €500. Because budget carriers rarely arrange alternate flights proactively, capping reimbursement at €80 leaves stranded passengers holding the bill for an airline’s failure to operate.

Source: EU Regulation 2026/2202 amending Regulation 261/2004

Destination

Information & Tips for Tanzania

The United Republic of Tanzania is a country in East Africa and probably best known by tourists for the semi-autonomous region Zanzibar. But also people that are into game drives will get their money’s worth in Tanzania since it is home to 4 big national parks. And if that’s not enough, you could still climb Mount Kilimanjaro, Africas highest mountain.

Best Time to Visit

There really is no right or wrong time to visit this well-loved location. That said, the best wildlife viewing months in Tanzania are during the Dry season from late June to October. The best chance of seeing the wildebeest migration in the Serengeti is during June and July and the time to see the wildebeest calving is late January to February.

Entry & Visa

All EU passport holders are eligible for a visa on arrival. The cost of a single-entry visa is about €50 for citizens of European countries.

item.content:encoded:
MSC Cruises is currently offering an affordable deal for a Western Mediterranean cruise. Departing on November 8, 2026, from Barcelona, you will spend a week aboard the MSC Sinfonia, calling at ports across Spain, France, and Italy.

Interior staterooms are currently bookable starting at just €399 per person. Additional options include oceanview staterooms from €499 and balcony cabins from €759 (based on double occupancy). Solo travelers can book an interior cabin starting from €556, representing a single supplement of roughly 40%.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form. We’re glad to help.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Looking to save even more on your booking? With our exclusive MSC coupon code, you can secure 5% cashback on the cruise fare (excluding mandatory hotel service charges). We have compiled a detailed walkthrough of how it works and how to redeem it during checkout here:

The Route

Your cruise begins in the Catalan capital of Barcelona. If you haven’t visited before, arriving a few days early is well worth it to explore Antoni Gaudí’s Sagrada Família and the lively tree-lined boulevard of Las Ramblas. The MSC Sinfonia casts off in the early evening.

The first port of call is Marseille. Take time to explore the Old Port (Vieux-Port), the historic heart of the city lined with cafes and seafood bistros. Another highlight is the hilltop Basilique Notre-Dame de la Garde, which sits 160 meters above the sea and provides sweeping coastal panoramas.

Next, the ship arrives in Genoa. The cruise terminal is situated directly adjacent to the city center, making it easy to explore the historic medieval alleyways on foot. Major sights include the 12th-century striped Cathedral of San Lorenzo and the Aquarium of Genoa.

The vessel continues to Livorno, which serves as the primary gateway for day trips to Florence and Pisa. From there, the MSC Sinfonia calls at Civitavecchia, allowing you to relax in the port town or take an excursion into Rome to visit the Colosseum, Roman Forum, St. Peter’s Basilica, and the Trevi Fountain.

The final port of call is Valencia, showcasing a mix of Spanish traditions and futuristic architecture, most notably Santiago Calatrava’s City of Arts and Sciences. After 7 nights, your voyage concludes back in Barcelona.

The Ship

Built in 2005 and lengthened during MSC’s Renaissance Program, the MSC Sinfonia measures 275 meters (902 feet) in length and 32 meters (105 feet) in beam. The vessel accommodates roughly 2,600 passengers alongside 700 crew members. Onboard facilities include 4 restaurants, 9 bars and lounges, 2 swimming pools, and 2 whirlpools. Beyond the MSC Aurea Spa and fitness center, recreational amenities include an outdoor jogging track, mini-golf, and a 600-seat theater. The primary onboard languages are English and Italian, and the onboard currency for Mediterranean sailings is the euro (€).

item.content:encoded:
Hotel voucher platform Animod is currently running an attractive deal for the Moxy Karlsruhe in southwestern Germany. Depending on your length of stay, you pay between €55 and €58 per night for a double room, with a full breakfast buffet included. The rate also includes complimentary on-site parking and late check-out (subject to availability).

Update: Free €20 Supermarket Voucher

It gets even better! Through the promotional link, every voucher purchase includes a complimentary €20 voucher for German discount supermarket chain Netto Marken-Discount. After purchasing, you must claim the voucher via bonus.animod.de, print it out, and redeem it by November 5, 2026.

Warning

Please note that the Animod website is only available in German. However, you can easily complete the purchase by using your browser’s built-in translation tool.

Show Deal

You can choose vouchers for 1, 2, or 3 nights. Including the local city tax of €4 per person per night, the total cost comes to:

  • 1 night for €58
  • 2 nights for €116
  • 3 nights for €164 (€55 / night)

You are purchasing an open-dated hotel voucher that is technically valid for redemption through October 2027. Currently, the online booking calendar has availability loaded through March 2027, with arrivals permitted Thursday through Sunday.

The Hotel

The Moxy Karlsruhe opened in September 2023 and features 150 guest rooms. Measuring 15 to 17 m² (161 to 183 sq ft), rooms follow Moxy’s signature minimalist design. There are no traditional wardrobes, but wall pegs and open hangers are provided. If you want to pull out your laptop to book your next travel deal, you’ll find a small stool and desk setup in the room.

However, working is much more comfortable in the vibrant lobby, which doubles as an open-concept co-working space with lounge seating, power outlets, and a foosball table. The property also features a 24/7 fitness center.

Location & Transportation

While Karlsruhe is well known across Germany as the seat of the Federal Constitutional Court, it is not a major tourist destination. The hotel is therefore particularly convenient for road-trippers or travelers in transit, supported by its location near the highway and complimentary on-site parking (subject to availability).

If arriving without a car, it is an 8-minute walk (600 meters) to the nearest tram and bus stop. From there, public transit reaches the city center, shopping districts, and Karlsruhe Palace in roughly 10 minutes. Getting to Karlsruhe Central Station (Hauptbahnhof) takes around 30 minutes with one transfer.

For groceries and travel essentials, an Aldi Süd supermarket and a dm drugstore are located directly next to the property.

Price Comparison

Pricing remains fairly consistent throughout autumn and winter. For comparison, we checked a weekend stay from November 13 to 14, 2026. On Animod, the €50 rate (+ €8 local city tax = €58 total) is available.

According to Trivago, the next cheapest booking channel charges €87 including city tax and breakfast. That equates to a 33% discount. If you treat the €20 Netto supermarket voucher as cash, your effective net cost drops to just €38 per night—saving over 50%!

Compared to booking directly with Marriott, the savings are even greater: Marriott charges €108 per night for the same date with breakfast included:

item.content:encoded:
The Costa Smeralda, one of the two flagship mega-ships in Italian cruise line Costa‘s fleet, will reposition to the Canary Islands and Madeira for the upcoming winter season. Before that deployment, you have the opportunity to take a week-long cruise through the Mediterranean. Departing from Barcelona on November 2, 2026, the voyage includes calls across Spain, Italy, and France.

Interior staterooms are currently bookable starting at just €499 per person, while oceanview cabins start at €549 (based on double occupancy). However, the standout value on this sailing is the balcony cabins starting from €599 per person—an upgrade costing less than €15 per person per night. Better yet, solo travelers pay no single supplement (0% surcharge) across all cabin categories.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form. We’re glad to help.

Show Deal

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Included Services

On Costa cruises, the standard cruise fare covers the following inclusions:

  • Full board dining across main dining rooms and buffet restaurants (specialty restaurants carry an additional charge)
  • Water, tea, and brewed coffee at breakfast, as well as dispenser water in buffet areas during opening hours
  • Crew gratuities and hotel service charges
  • Access to most onboard facilities (gym, pools, whirlpools, deck loungers, etc.)

On Costa ships, water, tea, and coffee are complimentary during breakfast in the main dining room and throughout buffet opening hours. During lunch and dinner in the main dining rooms—as well as across all specialty venues—all drinks, including water, must be purchased separately. For this reason, adding a beverage package can offer substantially better value on Costa than on many other cruise lines. Drink packages can be booked in advance via the MyCosta portal up to 48 hours before embarkation.

Costa offers the following optional beverage packages:

Costa Beverage Packages
  1. MySoft Drinks Package
    Starting from €23 per person per day (children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day).
    Includes unlimited non-alcoholic beverages served by the glass:
    • Coffee & tea specialties
    • Soft drinks and sodas
    • Energy drinks
  2. MyItalian Beverage Package
    €34.30 per adult per day (children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day for the non-alcoholic version); already included when booking the All Inclusive fare.
    Includes:
    • Tea, coffee specialties (including espresso and cappuccino), water, soft drinks, and juices
    • Draft beer, aperitifs, and standard cocktails (excluding solid, molecular, and ultra-premium cocktails)
    • Selection of wines by the glass, spirits, and liqueurs
    • One 0.5-liter bottle of mineral water per adult per day (not applicable to children), convenient for shore days
    • Unlimited gelato (maximum 2 scoops per order)
    • One complimentary pizza per cruise at the Pummid’Oro Pizzeria (excluding “Gourmet” tier pizzas)
  3. MyItalian Plus Beverage Package
    €45.80 per adult per day (children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day for the non-alcoholic version); already included when booking a Suite under the All Inclusive fare.
    Includes all perks of the MyItalian package, plus:
    • Molecular and premium top-shelf cocktails
    • Bottled beers (such as Corona and Beck’s)
    • Unlimited bottled mineral water (0.5-liter bottles)
    • In-cabin minibar beverages
    • Looza bottled fruit juices

Alternatively, Costa offers fixed-quantity drink voucher bundles, such as 20 draft beers (0.4L) for €105 (€5.25/glass) or 13 bottles of mineral water (1L) for €42 (€3.23/bottle). These bundles can also be purchased prior to embarkation through the MyCosta portal.

The Route

The cruise sets sail from Barcelona. The vibrant Catalan capital remains a beloved destination year-round, highlighted by Antoni Gaudí’s Sagrada Família and the bustling tree-lined boulevard of Las Ramblas.

The first port of call is Cagliari. In Sardinia’s capital, head up to Piazza Palazzo for the finest panoramic views over the city and bay. Other notable sights include the National Archaeological Museum and the Baroque Church of Sant’Efisio. Next, the ship calls at Palermo, Sicily. The Teatro Massimo, Italy’s largest opera house, sits directly en route into the historic center. Palermo Cathedral is equally stunning with its blend of Arab, Norman, and Gothic architecture—climbing to the cathedral roof yields panoramic vistas over the Sicilian capital.

The following stop is Civitavecchia, located roughly an hour from Rome. Booking a cruise line excursion or taking the regional train allows you to explore the Colosseum, St. Peter’s Basilica, and the Spanish Steps without rushing.

The Costa Smeralda then docks in Savona. The imposing 16th-century Priamàr Fortress crowns the waterfront, dominating the coastline. Following a final port call in Marseille, the ship returns to Barcelona after a week at sea.

The Ship

The Costa Smeralda, launched in 2020, accommodates up to 5,200 passengers. With a gross tonnage of 182,000, the ship measures 337 meters in length, and 36 meters in width, and features a draft of 8 meters. It boasts 18 decks and was constructed at the Meyer Turku shipyard in Finland, with a building cost of approximately $950 million.

The ship features 15 restaurants, including Chinese and Japanese options. Six are included in the cruise fare, offering basic dining experiences (main dining rooms and buffets). Three areas are reserved for suites, club members, or families. Six premium dining venues are available for an additional charge, providing higher-quality cuisine in exclusive settings.

Throughout the public decks, there are 19 bars, as well as amenities like a cinema, theatre, shopping centre, casino, pool deck (with a covered pool for cooler days), fitness centre, water slide, disco, aqua park, and a kids’ club.

Destination

Information & Tips for Delhi

Delhi, India’s capital, is known for historic sites like the Red Fort, Humayun’s Tomb, and Qutub Minar, as well as vibrant markets and cultural districts. The local currency is the Indian rupee (INR), and cash is widely used, though cards and digital payments are increasingly common. Prices are generally low by international standards, making it a budget-friendly destination. The weather is extreme—very hot in summer (April–June), with a monsoon season from July to September, and cooler, more comfortable weather from October to March.

item.dc:creator: Peer
item.description: Travel to Japan continues to boom. Last year, the country welcomed over 400,000 visitors from Germany alone (source), significantly surpassing pre-pandemic figures. item.content:encoded:
Travel to Japan continues to boom. Last year, the country welcomed over 400,000 visitors from Germany alone (source), significantly surpassing pre-pandemic figures. With demand remaining strong, many European travelers also prefer to avoid connecting via Middle Eastern hubs due to geopolitical uncertainties.

Lufthansa is seizing this opportunity by significantly expanding its network to Japan. For the summer 2027 schedule, the German carrier will resume two previously suspended routes. Departing from Frankfurt, flights will once again head to Nagoya and Tokyo-Narita multiple times per week.

Three Flights Weekly from Frankfurt to Nagoya

While Nagoya in Aichi Prefecture is not primarily known as a major tourist destination, it is one of Japan’s most important industrial and economic hubs. Lufthansa previously served the destination until Frankfurt – Nagoya was suspended in 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic. An initially planned resumption for 2024 never materialized.

Now, the route is set to make a definitive comeback. Starting March 29, 2027—just in time for cherry blossom season—Lufthansa plans to operate three weekly flights. Service will be operated by Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners fitted with the Allegris cabin interior. The configuration features 28 seats in business class (including 4 front-row suites), 28 seats in premium economy (arranged 2-3-2), and 231 seats in economy class (arranged 3-3-3).

The flights are scheduled seasonally (March through October) according to the following timetable:

  • Frankfurt → Nagoya (Mon, Wed, Sat):
    • LH 736 Frankfurt FRA → Nagoya NGO: 14:10 – 09:35 (+1)
  • Nagoya → Frankfurt (Tue, Thu, Sun):
    • LH 737 Nagoya NGO → Frankfurt FRA: 11:30 – 18:30

Lufthansa is not the only European carrier flying to Nagoya; Finnair also operates seasonal summer flights between Helsinki and Nagoya.

Daily Flights from Frankfurt to Tokyo-Narita

Following an absence of nearly a decade, Lufthansa is also reinstating flights between Frankfurt and Tokyo’s Narita Airport. This route is somewhat less groundbreaking: Lufthansa already flies to the much more convenient Tokyo-Haneda Airport, and Frankfurt – Narita is served non-stop by Japan Airlines. The Oneworld carrier generally provides a superior passenger experience in almost every category (with the possible exception of the business class hard product).

In any case, Lufthansa will offer daily service on the Frankfurt – Tokyo-Narita route starting March 28, 2027. This service will also be operated by Boeing 787-9 aircraft with the Allegris configuration. Flights are currently filed as seasonal, running through late October.

The timetable:

  • Frankfurt → Tokyo (Daily):
    • LH 710 Frankfurt FRA → Tokyo NRT: 13:45 – 09:30 (+1)
  • Tokyo → Frankfurt (Tue, Thu, Sun):
    • LH 711 Tokyo NRT → Frankfurt FRA: 11:20 – 18:40

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Flights Already Open for Booking

All of the routes above are already open for booking on Lufthansa.com for the summer 2027 season. However, current fares are prohibitively expensive: even an economy class round-trip currently prices out at over €1,500, while business class commands more than €5,000.

Award redemptions would be far more appealing, though award inventory on these two “new” routes appears unreleased for now. For a one-way award ticket in business class, expect to redeem around 66,000 miles alongside €400 to €500 in (recently increased) carrier surcharges. You can always book to Haneda instead of Narita (or via Zurich on Swiss)—and for most leisure travelers, Haneda is the vastly superior airport due to its central location:

item.content:encoded:
Setting sail on May 31, 2027, the MS Europa embarks on a 16-night luxury voyage from Nice to Hamburg, calling at ports across Spain, France, Portugal, and Belgium. Fares for this sailing were reduced today by roughly €2,400 per person. You can currently book a suite starting from €5,733 per person based on double occupancy. This promotional rate is unfortunately not available for solo travelers.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form. We’re glad to help.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Included Services

On board Hapag-Lloyd Cruises vessels, guests enjoy the following complimentary inclusions:

  • Full board dining across various gourmet restaurants
  • All-day non-alcoholic beverages and coffee specialties
  • All in-suite beverages (minibar replenished daily)
  • Welcome champagne upon arrival in your suite
  • Onboard cultural program with evening entertainment and performances
  • 24-hour room service
  • Zodiac landings and excursions (destination-dependent)
  • Access to the interactive Ocean Academy (on expedition vessels)
  • One hour of complimentary internet access per person per day
  • German-speaking tour management and staff

The Route

The voyage begins in Nice, with the vessel casting off from Villefranche-sur-Mer along the French Riviera. Following a relaxing sea day, you reach Valencia. Standout highlights include the historic cathedral, the UNESCO-listed silk exchange (La Lonja de la Seda), and the Central Market, set in contrast to the futuristic City of Arts and Sciences.

Following another day at sea, the ship calls at Marbella on the Costa del Sol. The charming old town with its narrow whitewashed alleys, flowering balconies, and the Plaza de los Naranjos is ideal for an afternoon stroll. You can also walk down Avenida del Mar to the seaside promenade, or take a day trip to nearby Málaga or the mountain village of Mijas.

Another day at sea offers time to unwind before the ship docks overnight in Lisbon. Portugal’s capital is easily explored on foot or aboard historic tram 28. Famous landmarks include the historic Alfama quarter, Praça do Comércio, the Belém Tower, and the Jerónimos Monastery.

After another sea day, you arrive in A Coruña in northwestern Spain. The city’s signature monument is the Tower of Hercules, the world’s oldest functioning Roman lighthouse. The sweeping waterfront promenade, Plaza de María Pita, and the old town invite leisurely exploration. Regional excursions lead to the pilgrimage cathedral of Santiago de Compostela.

Following a sea day crossing the Bay of Biscay, the ship calls at Saint-Malo in Brittany. Completely encircled by preserved granite ramparts, walking along the city walls offers sweeping views of coastal islands. Longer excursions lead to Cancale, celebrated for fresh Breton oysters.

The route continues to Honfleur at the mouth of the Seine. The picturesque historic harbor (Vieux Bassin), narrow slate-fronted townhouses, and the wooden Sainte-Catherine church define the town’s artistic heritage. Nearby day trips explore upscale coastal resorts like Deauville and Trouville-sur-Mer.

From Honfleur, the vessel sails to Antwerp, Belgium. World-renowned for Flemish architecture, historic diamond trading, and a vibrant port, highlights include the Grote Markt, the Cathedral of Our Lady, the monumental Antwerpen-Centraal station, and the Museum aan de Stroom (MAS). After a final day at sea, the cruise concludes in Hamburg.

The Ship

The MS Europa was built in 1999 and underwent an extensive multi-million-euro revitalization in 2024. Measuring 199 meters in length and 24 meters in width with a cruising speed of up to 21 knots, the vessel maintains an intimate, uncrowded luxury atmosphere. With a maximum of just 400 guests attended to by 285 crew members, the ship delivers one of the highest staff-to-guest ratios in the industry. For over two decades, the Berlitz Cruise Guide has consistently ranked the MS Europa as one of the world’s premier 5-star-plus luxury vessels.

Accommodations consist entirely of spacious suites ranging from 27 m² up to 85 m² in the grand penthouse categories. Many suites feature separate living and sleeping quarters as well as walk-in wardrobes with vanity tables. The in-suite minibar is completely complimentary and replenished daily with your preferred beverages.

Fine dining is central to the MS Europa experience, led by internationally acclaimed chefs across multiple complimentary culinary venues. Highlights include the flagship Europa Restaurant, modern culinary artistry at The Globe by Kevin Fehling (a 3-star Michelin chef), sophisticated French seafood at Pearls, and authentic Italian dining at Venezia. For a casual meal, the Lido Café offers indoor and outdoor buffet dining alongside an open grill station.

Wellness and leisure facilities include a heated open-air swimming pool on the lido deck, the comprehensive Ocean Spa offering saunas and treatments, and a panoramic fitness center offering scheduled fitness classes and one-on-one personal training sessions.

item.content:encoded:
While traditional airline mileage bargains have become less frequent at programs like Miles&More, monthly award discounts remain alive and well elsewhere. Through its recurring Privilege Deals promotion, Qatar Airways offers a 25% discount on standard Avios redemption rates across selected routes.

This month’s offers are bookable until October 31, 2026 for travel through November 30, 2026. You can book one-way business class awards connecting from Germany to the Middle East starting at just 33,750 Avios (+ €210 in taxes and surcharges), or fly from Warsaw to Australia and New Zealand starting from 67,500 Avios (+ €304).

Show Deal

In business class and first class, promotional award rates apply to flights to and from the following destinations:

  • Bucharest (OTP)
  • Warsaw (WAW)
  • Ankara (ESB)
  • Tunis (TUN)
  • Zanzibar (ZNZ)
  • Jeddah (JED)
  • Amman (AMM)
  • Yerevan (EVN)
  • Medina (MED)
  • Salalah (SLL)
Award Search Tip

If you have trouble finding award space on your preferred dates via the standard search engine, try using Qatar’s dedicated Award Flight Finder. While it works most reliably on direct segments (and does not display live prices), it helps identify days with standard award availability.

Examples: Business Class from 33,750 Miles + €210

Qatar Airways levies carrier-imposed fuel surcharges in addition to statutory government taxes. However, compared to other major European carriers, these cash co-payments remain relatively moderate. With the 25% Avios discount applied, several attractive redemption options emerge.

Below are sample one-way connections (all routing via Doha):

Business class:

  • Salalah → Munich for 33,750 Avios + €210
  • Berlin → Salalah for 33,750 Avios + €231 (with 14h in Doha)
  • Berlin → Zanzibar for 48,750 Avios + €313
  • Warsaw → Osaka for 60,000 Avios + €215
  • Warsaw → Adelaide for 67,500 Avios + €304 (with 21h in Doha)
  • Warsaw → Auckland for 67,500 Avios + €344 (with 21h in Doha)

Mixed-cabin business + first class:

  • Warsaw → Dubai for 33,750 Avios + €198
    (business class on Warsaw – Doha, regional “first class” on Doha – Dubai)
  • Munich → Jeddah for 33,750 Avios + €251
    (business class on Munich – Doha, regional “first class” on Doha – Jeddah)

On regional short hops (such as flights within the Gulf), regional first class primarily features standard recliner seats similar to short-haul business class. However, a major perk is complimentary access to Qatar Airways’ flagship Al Safwa First Class Lounge during your transit in Doha.

The 25% discount is deducted automatically when available. You will also see a promotional notification banner above the calendar in the flexible +/- 3-day search view:

Terms & Conditions

  • Booking period: Through October 31, 2026
  • Travel period: Departures through November 30, 2026
  • Applies to connecting flights: the total required Avios sum across all legs is reduced by 25%
  • Not valid on Flexi Awards (double-priced awards for expanded inventory)
  • Standard cancellation terms apply: cancellable for a US$25 fee up to 24 hours prior to departure, or US$100 up to 3 hours prior
  • Accounts must be at least 30 days old to book award tickets (the previous restriction requiring at least one credited cash flight was lifted in September)
  • Qatar Airways categorizes dates into Off-Peak and Peak periods. The 25% discount applies to both, though peak dates require roughly 20% more base Avios
  • Valid exclusively on flights operated by Qatar Airways or marketed under a Qatar Airways flight number
  • Bookings must be completed through Qatar Airways Privilege Club. Avios can be linked and transferred 1:1 instantly from British Airways, Iberia, or Finnair at no charge.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Depending on the route, flights are operated by one of three aircraft types: Embraer regional jets, the Airbus A320 family, or the Boeing 737.

On Embraer 190/195 aircraft, economy class seats are arranged in a 2-2 configuration with no middle seats, and seat pitch is approximately 79 cm. These jets are typically used on shorter or lower-demand routes.

Aircraft from the Airbus A320 family (such as the A319 and A320) and the Boeing 737 feature a 3-3 configuration in economy, with an average seat pitch of around 76 cm.

While low-cost carriers like Wizz Air also fly to Belgrade, Air Serbia includes several valuable perks that basic low-cost tickets lack:

  • Free airport check-in
  • Standard overhead cabin bag up to 8 kg (55 x 40 x 23 cm)
  • Personal item up to 4 kg (e.g. laptop bag or small backpack fitting under the seat in front)
  • Complimentary cup of water and a small snack

By contrast, while Wizz Air may advertise base fares around €50, adding a full-size overhead carry-on bag alone can cost up to €30 extra each way due to their dynamic ancillary pricing.

Visa & Entry Requirements

EU, UK, and US passport holders do not require a visa for tourism stays of up to 90 days within any 180-day window. Note that Serbian border authorities factor time spent in Kosovo into this allowance. Always check your national foreign ministry’s official travel advisory for current entry rules.

Search & Book

According to the fare rules, this deal is valid until October 11, 2026. Travel is available from November 2026 through August 2027, with slight date variations depending on your departure city.

There is no minimum stay requirement. You can scout dates easily using Google Flights.

Miles & Points

No mileage accrual is possible in the Light fare. Air Serbia’s previous loyalty partnership with Etihad Guest was terminated effective June 30, 2026.

Our availability calendar highlights all possible flight dates at the lowest price for trips up to 28 days. It will forward you to EasyJet with your selected flight dates.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

EasyJet operates aircraft with a 3-3 seating configuration and a narrow seat pitch. The flight takes approximately three hours. Complimentary food and drinks are not provided, so travelers may wish to purchase refreshments before boarding or on the aircraft.

Visa Info

Most European passport holders need a visa for Egypt, which can be purchased on arrival for US$30 (~€27). Alternatively, a free 15-day Sinai-only visa is available if you only stay in the Sinai resort area (e.g. Sharm El Sheikh).

Search & Book

This deal does not have a set expiration date, but low fares are subject to availability and can change at any time. Departures are scattered until June 2027 with most occurring between December 2026 and February 2027.

You can find suitable dates using our calendar above or with the help of Google Flights. We recommend booking directly on EasyJet’s website.

Destination

Information & Tips for Egypt

Egypt is best known for ancient sites such as the Pyramids of Giza, the temples of Luxor and Karnak, and the Nile Valley, with Cairo also offering major museums and busy urban life. The local currency is the Egyptian pound (EGP), and everyday costs are generally low by international standards, especially for food, transport, and local services, while hotels and guided tours can vary widely in price. The climate is mostly hot and dry, with very high temperatures in summer, mild winters, and little rainfall outside the Mediterranean coast.

Egypt’s transport infrastructure is functional but uneven. In major cities like Cairo and Alexandria, getting around is possible via metros, buses, minibuses, and ride-hailing apps, though congestion and crowding are common. Between cities, trains run along the Nile Valley and to Alexandria and are generally the most practical option, while long-distance buses and domestic flights fill in gaps, especially for resort areas. Travel is usually manageable with some planning, but comfort and reliability can vary.
